title: Tens of thousands march across Germany to protest far-right party AfD
summary: Protesters in about 20 cities, including Berlin, Hamburg and Munich, demand the banning of the Alternative for Germany.

title: Only Roland Garros towel left, says Ukraine tennis player after Russian strike hits flat
summary: Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.

title: Bahrain says it will not participate in Iran’s proposed Hormuz meeting
summary: Iran tells Al Jazeera that Monday's meeting is a sign of 'good intentions' towards neighbouring countries.

title: Will Houthi advances in Yemen give Iran leverage in its war with the US?
summary: The Iranian ally seizes Yemen's Red Sea coast, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

title: Iraq probes drone strikes on Saudi Arabia, shuts three crossings to Iran
summary: PM Ali al-Zaidi dismisses commander, orders investigation into operations command in Maysan province, bordering Iran.

title: Iran, UAE hold first talks at BRICS summit since conflict began
summary: Iran’s President has met Abu Dhabi’s Crown Prince at the BRICS summit for their highest-level talks since the war began.

title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage
summary: Officials are not ruling out "outside interference", while the company says the blaze at its site was sabotage.

title: Selling the war: Purges, polygraphs and propaganda
summary: The Iran war has become ever more challenging for the Trump administration to sell.

title: Couple welcomes child from embryo frozen for 22 years
summary: A Greek couple has welcomed a child using an embryo frozen for 22 years.

title: Will the Houthi attacks activate the Mecca Pact?
summary: If there is a Saudi request, Pakistan and Turkiye will intervene, but direct involvement in the Yemen war is unlikely.

title: US court rejects Trump’s emergency order keeping Michigan coal plant open
summary: The ruling says the Energy Department exceeded its authority by extending the plant’s operation.

title: At least seven killed in fire at prison in northern Syria
summary: Inmates rioted following protests in the city of Kobane over the killing of former Kurdish fighter, state media reports.

title: Danish FA allege FIFA Legal Committee evaded questions on Infantino’s plan
summary: FIFA Legal Committee accused of evading questions on controversial World Cup proposal put forward by Gianni Infantino.

title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
summary: Iraq removes a military commander and opens investigations into the attack that came from an area bordering Iran.

title: Ukraine faces 'toughest winter' since Russia's full-scale invasion, UN official tells BBC
summary: A senior UN official tells the BBC there is a race against the clock to ensure access to power and water through winter.

title: Firefighters say this antioxidant helped them - their union warns it could be risky
summary: Glutathione, an antioxidant, has been offered as a treatment at some of the largest US wildfires in recent years.

title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe
summary: Art crime investigators and security experts say burglaries from galleries across Europe are becoming more brazen.

title: Lightning Houthi advance in Yemen may bring dangerous new dimension to Iran war
summary: The capture by the rebels of a stretch of Yemen's strategic coastline is the group's most impressive military coup for several years.

title: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors mark 9/11 with counter-terrorism push on AI and drones
summary: The Security Council met to mark 25 years since the 9/11 attacks with a briefing on counter-terrorism as ambassadors take stock of a threat that has morphed dramatically since resolution 1373 built the council's counter-terrorism machinery in 2001. Briefers highlighted militants' growing use of artificial intelligence, drones and encrypted platforms for recruitment and attack planning.

title: Terrorist propaganda is outpacing global efforts to stop it, UN report finds
summary: Terrorist groups are recruiting, raising money and even planning operations through propaganda that is now “embedded” in every stage of their work, a new UN report warns – and governments are struggling to keep pace.

title: Ukraine: Drone attacks on Chornobyl are ‘gambling with the safety of millions of people’
summary: A drone strike on the protective structure at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant could have endangered the safety of millions of people, UN Development Programme (UNDP) Administrator Alexander De Croo told reporters via video link from Kyiv on Thursday.

title: UN climate chief warns political division is undermining fight against ‘economic security emergency’
summary: The head of the UN's climate body has warned that treating global warming as a partisan issue is dangerously out of step with reality, as he set out a stark account of the economic toll climate change is already inflicting on Europe.

title: Security Council LIVE: Fresh attacks prompt emergency meeting on Yemen
summary: On the heels of reported Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on Tuesday and the capture of another key port by the militants on Yemen’s Red Sea coast – including the seizure of eight UN vehicles from a key aid hub there – the Security Council is meeting on Thursday at 3pm in New York to discuss the latest developments.

title: UN hails Libya election deal as Security Council urges Libyans to seize the moment
summary: The UN Security Council has welcomed a breakthrough agreement between Libya's rival political blocs, calling it "an important step" towards the country's first national elections in over a decade – while pressing all sides to move quickly from paper to practice.

title: Guterres urges leaders to invest in peace as conflicts deepen
summary: The UN Secretary-General appealed on Wednesday for world leaders to invest in peace as violence, division and conflict exacerbate suffering worldwide.

title: Record number of attacks on education, global fund warns
summary: While September traditionally marks the start of the school year across the northern hemisphere, a staggering 93 million children are not in class at all amid an unprecedented number of attacks on learning, education experts warned on Wednesday.

title: Ships and seafarers increasingly caught in the crossfire of unrelated wars
summary: The global shipping industry is facing a "genuinely unprecedented" convergence of maritime crises, with vessels and seafarers increasingly used as “leverage” in conflicts that have nothing to do with them.

title: AI datacentres pose growing threat to electricity systems worldwide
summary: Use of data-intensive technologies – in particular artificial intelligence (AI) data centres – is growing faster than electricity infrastructure can handle, the UN’s economic commission for Europe has warned, raising concerns about the future reliability and resilience of energy systems worldwide.

title: ‘This is not 1945’: General Assembly president gavels open new session aimed at restoring global trust
summary: The UN General Assembly gavelled open its 81st session on Tuesday at UN Headquarters as the incoming president pledged to restore public trust in the institution during a time of war, humanitarian crises and intensifying climate change.

title: In Gaza, women-headed households face ‘impossible choices’ to survive
summary: In war-torn Gaza, a growing number of women-headed households face “impossible decisions” every day, amid ongoing Israeli airstrikes and still-scarce resources, UN humanitarians said on Tuesday.

title: Tobacco use can undermine fertility, UN health agency warns
summary: Smoking very likely makes it harder to have a baby, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned in a new publication issued on Tuesday, highlighting that women who smoke have a 40 per cent higher risk of infertility compared to non-smokers.

title: AI: Türk urges action before it becomes an ‘existential risk to humanity’
summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk added his voice on Monday to growing calls for greater AI controls, warning that the revolutionary technology could become an “existential risk to humanity” if left unchecked.

title: Human rights chief Türk renews call for end to spiralling Sudan war
summary: The ongoing war in Sudan took centre stage at the UN Human Rights Council on Monday where the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, led calls for an end to attacks on civilians in “markets, hospitals [and] fuel stations”.

title: Coordinated action on clean air and climate change can net $15 for every dollar spent
summary: Tackling air pollution and climate change together can save millions of lives, reduce global warming and generate roughly $15 in economic benefits for every $1 spent, a new UN-backed report has revealed.

title: ‘Advance safety for all’: International police cooperation helps tackle cross-border crime
summary: As criminal networks increasingly exploit weak institutions and operate across borders, the UN says no police force can tackle them alone.
